name: Chinese unification
summary: Chinese unification, as Beijing advances it, holds that Taiwan is an inseparable part of China and that the divided state left by the civil war must be reunified, preferably peacefully under one country, two systems, but with force reserved against secession or foreign interference. It ties unification to national rejuvenation and treats the question as purely internal. It is a single-issue territorial doctrine, so it says little on economic, social or cultural questions.
scope: The People's Republic of China's official unification doctrine from Deng Xiaoping's one country, two systems through the 2005 Anti-Secession Law and the 2022 white paper under Xi Jinping. It excludes the Republic of China/KMT version, in which unification would occur under the ROC, and pro-unification currents in Taiwan that differ from Beijing's formula. Statements outside the Taiwan question are mostly inferred from general PRC state doctrine and marked low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent on health policy; the white paper promises equal treatment for Taiwan residents, and PRC state doctrine favours state-provided welfare, so mild agreement is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The unification program says nothing on wages and Beijing's line is mixed, so adherents have no stated position here.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Official PRC doctrine keeps a state-led economy with markets under party direction; one-country-two-systems preserves Taiwan's capitalism but does not claim markets beat governments.

public-ownership.rationale: Mainland doctrine keeps public ownership dominant while promising Taiwan its own economic system, so unification adherents are split or indifferent on the question.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Nothing in unification doctrine bears on taxation of the wealthy; one-country-two-systems explicitly leaves Taiwan's fiscal system alone.

unions-good.rationale: Not addressed; PRC doctrine favours state-sanctioned unions only, and the unification program is silent.

property-fundamental.rationale: The white paper pledges to protect private property in Taiwan after unification, but the mainland system does not treat property as a near-inviolable right, so no firm stance.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program; no clear adherent position is documented.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which treats welfare as a state responsibility rather than a dependency problem; unification texts are silent.

worker-ownership.rationale: Mainland doctrine favours state and mixed ownership rather than worker-owned firms, and the unification program does not endorse worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the state's security-first posture (the Anti-Secession Law prioritises countering separatism); unification texts do not address surveillance directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; PRC state policy is strict prohibition, which is the inferred position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The white paper attacks separatist propaganda and "de-sinicization", but this is not a hate-speech doctrine, so no clear stance.

strong-leader.rationale: Deng's framework has Beijing intervening when needed and the party centralised under a paramount leader; inferred, not a unification tenet.

state-harmful.rationale: Unification is a state-building project: the law makes reunification a state duty and authorises the State Council and military to enforce it.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in unification texts; PRC state policy bans civilian gun ownership, so mild agreement inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Article 8 authorises military force as a last resort and the white paper refuses to renounce it, implying support for strong armed forces.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; PRC law prohibits sex work, which is the inferred state position.

decide-locally.rationale: Unification rests on a single sovereign centre; Taiwan would be a special administrative region with autonomy only as granted under one China.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed by unification doctrine; no basis for a position.

traditional-family.rationale: The white paper stresses shared Chinese culture and heritage across the Strait, from which mild support for traditional values is inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent, and Taiwan's legal same-sex marriage is not cited as an obstacle; adherents are indifferent.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

more-religion-public.rationale: The white paper promises freedom of religious belief in Taiwan but mainland doctrine keeps religion under state supervision; inferred mild disagreement.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; unification doctrine has no racial-justice program.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The white paper frames shared Chinese identity and culture as the basis of unification and opposes "de-sinicization" in Taiwan.

gradual-change.rationale: Unification is pursued in "steps and phases" but the aim is radical change in the Strait's status, so this general claim does not map cleanly.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The white paper rejects external interference and treats the Taiwan question as purely internal, opposing UN or foreign roles in it.

free-trade.rationale: The white paper promotes cross-Strait economic integration and a common market, but state doctrine is not a general free-trade creed.

nation-first.rationale: The white paper subordinates cross-strait and international considerations to sovereignty, territorial integrity and national rejuvenation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Article 3 and the white paper insist the Taiwan question is purely internal with no outside interference, a principle of non-intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on sovereignty and territorial borders; unification doctrine treats borders as defining state integrity.

limit-growth.rationale: National rejuvenation is tied to development and growth; unification texts do not address environmental limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

revolution-justified.rationale: The CCP was founded by revolution but the law targets secession as unlawful and states the PRC's legitimacy as settled; inferred mild disagreement for present-day politics.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not addressed; no clear adherent position.

central-planning.rationale: Mainland doctrine now favours a socialist market economy; the unification program does not address planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; the unification program preserves Taiwan's own economic system.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; the white paper offers economic integration and favourable trade for Taiwan rather than a tariff doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from PRC state-led development practice; the white paper proposes state-backed integration projects such as a Fujian pilot zone.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The white paper promises protection of Taiwan's private property, but takes no stance on property distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Official doctrine is a socialist market economy; abolition of money is a distant aim not pursued in the unification program.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from state-led economic doctrine; unification texts do not address central banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

one-party-rule.rationale: The unification program is a CCP policy and Beijing's one-country-two-systems rests on party-led central authority, though the Taiwan question itself does not require this answer.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred from republican state doctrine; not addressed in unification texts.

democracy-best.rationale: Beijing claims its system is a "whole-process democracy" but Deng held Western-style systems unsuitable; adherents give no clear endorsement.

direct-votes.rationale: Beijing's approach to Taiwan rests on negotiation among authorities, not referendums, and rejects plebiscites on status; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Not part of the unification program; state doctrine rests on party-led institutions.

right-to-secede.rationale: Article 2 states secession will not be allowed under any name or by any means, and Article 8 authorises force against it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

political-violence-never.rationale: Article 8 and the white paper explicitly keep the option of force against secession, so violence is not ruled out.

war-builds-character.rationale: Beijing presents force as a last resort and Article 9 stresses minimizing losses, so it does not celebrate war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred from secular state doctrine; unification texts are silent on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state alone holds the military decision under Article 8 (State Council and Central Military Commission), so private defence is rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: Credible force against Taiwan independence is the backstop of the policy in Article 8 and the white paper, implying military strength relative to rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The white paper frames the Chinese nation as a shared kinship and heritage across the Strait, though the PRC officially recognises many ethnic groups.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Unification doctrine frames history as national division and rejuvenation, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The white paper treats Taiwan as a unitary part of China; autonomy is state-granted, not by indigenous rights. Inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The white paper cites Japanese colonial rule and Taiwan's cession but takes no clear stance on reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Beijing grounds unification in shared Chinese civilisation and history spanning both sides of the Strait; the statement is general but fits that logic.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Collective national interest is prioritised in state doctrine; inferred from the framing of reunification as a shared duty of all Chinese (Article 4).

duties-before-rights.rationale: Article 4 frames reunification as a sacred duty of all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots, placing national obligation first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred from national-rejuvenation framing, which treats modernisation as positive.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from state security doctrine; unification texts silent.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rejuvenation is both restoring historical unity and forward progress, so adherents see no tradeoff to choose between.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Not addressed; Deng's pragmatism favours results, but the unification line is framed as principle.

direct-action.rationale: The law channels change through state authority and negotiation (Article 7), not direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred from national rejuvenation and development goals; unification texts are silent.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of the unification program.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

production-for-use.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The white paper promises Taiwan capitalism would be preserved after unification, which contradicts treating profit as exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Not addressed; unification texts do not invoke it.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the mainland's post-collective rural reforms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; the white paper blames outside powers' interference, not capitalism as such.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred from state doctrine; not addressed in unification texts.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Article 4 frames duty to nation and Article 6 protects residents' rights, but national interest takes priority over individual claims. Inferred.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from the state's mobilisation under Article 8 and the PRC's conscription law; unification texts do not address it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not part of unification doctrine; Beijing's approach insists on binding, not exit-based, sovereignty.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

media-academia-power.rationale: The white paper blames separatist propaganda for identity problems but does not make a claim about media power generally.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; official line is ethnic unity among Chinese, not a race-science doctrine.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

total-state.rationale: Not addressed; one-country-two-systems explicitly allows distinct systems, which cuts against a total-state reading.

national-rebirth.rationale: The white paper says reunification is essential to the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, the central justification.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Beijing frames Taiwan as recovering existing territory, not expansion, so adherents would reject the label but support retaking.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

single-common-good.rationale: The white paper frames unification as in the common interest of all Chinese people, a single national good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed beyond the white paper's calls for Taiwan compatriots to share in the nation.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

economic-freedom.rationale: Deng argued political systems need not match economic systems; inferred rejection of the claim that political freedom needs economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

national-self-determination.rationale: The white paper claims the Chinese nation's right to a unified state while denying Taiwan's separate self-determination, so the general principle is read as applying to the whole Chinese nation.

force-without-un.rationale: Article 8 authorises force on Beijing's own decision, and the white paper rejects outside authority over the Taiwan question.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

class-collaboration.rationale: Official doctrine stresses social harmony; inferred, not a unification tenet.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The white paper opposes de-sinicization and treats shared cultural heritage as the basis of unity.

dominated-front.rationale: The white paper accuses the US of using Taiwan to contain China and calls on others to oppose hegemonism; a common front is inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred from market-based financial system on both sides; not addressed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Unification doctrine asserts one Chinese nation and equal treatment of Taiwan residents, incompatible with legal racial separation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

national-mission.rationale: The white paper rejects exporting a system and says Taiwan keeps its own; it asks for no spread of the mainland model abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The white paper attacks Taiwan's pro-independence authorities, but does not denounce political elites generally.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; inferred disagreement from official stance.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state doctrine that does not accept external accountability for security forces.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Anti-Secession Law gives the state wide duties of economic, cultural and security integration (Articles 5, 6), not a minimal role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Unification doctrine seeks closer ties and integration among all Chinese, rejecting this.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The white paper promises equal treatment of Taiwan compatriots, but the statement is general; mild agreement inferred.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Official doctrine is socialism with Chinese characteristics in one country; the unification program does not invoke world revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed beyond the white paper's account of Taiwan's colonial past.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: One-country-two-systems preserves separate legal systems for Hong Kong, Macau and a unified Taiwan, a form of legal pluralism by region.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The white paper stresses a strong state and countering hostile external forces, but it is not framed in Marxist terms; inferred mild agreement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Beijing rejects a Taiwanese vote on status: the white paper treats unification as a national matter, though it promises consultation.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

population-transfer.rationale: Article 9 commits to protecting Taiwan civilians and residents, which excludes forced removal.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Article 8 authorises the state to initiate force under stated conditions and the white paper refuses to renounce it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The law bars secession "under any name or by any means" and Beijing bans pro-independence politics at home; it supports outlawing such parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

separated-powers.rationale: Official doctrine rejects Western separation of powers; unification texts do not address it, so inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: CCP doctrine; the unification program is a party policy but does not itself restate vanguardism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Article 8 authorises extraordinary measures in a secession crisis, so emergency powers are inferred to be acceptable.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

party-controls-media.rationale: CCP media control is documented practice; unification texts attack separatist propaganda but do not discuss media control itself.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Central Military Commission, a party body, decides on force in Article 8, reflecting party command of the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: CCP democratic centralism; not specific to the unification program.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The white paper says sovereignty is indivisible and rejects any "two Chinas" or EU-style arrangement; Beijing rejected such proposals.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred from nationalist doctrine of national unity in conflict.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The white paper opposes foreign military involvement around Taiwan, but it is about US alliances rather than a general policy; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from professional-army doctrine.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The central aim: the white paper and Article 4 call national reunification the duty of all Chinese, treating the 1949 division as a civil-war remnant.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

death-penalty.rationale: PRC retains capital punishment, but the unification program does not address it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular state education.

restrict-pornography.rationale: PRC bans pornography; unification texts silent.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The white paper treats Taiwan residents as Chinese compatriots by descent and nation, so descent-based membership is inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Unification is negotiated between authorities under one China, not through a new constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Deng argued that stability precedes development and Western-style political systems are unsuitable; inferred from Deng's framing in one-country-two-systems.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: PRC maintains its own deterrent; unification texts do not address it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; PRC head of state is chosen by the legislature.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; PRC central bank is under the State Council.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial integrity is non-negotiable in Article 2; Beijing treats Taiwan as national territory that it will not give up.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from socialist doctrine; not addressed in unification texts.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; official PRC line treats the Soviet period as socialist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

collective-defense.rationale: The white paper opposes foreign military alliances and US defence commitments toward Taiwan as interference.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Beijing denies Taiwan is annexed territory, and calls Hong Kong and Taiwan matters internal; inferred disagreement.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Article 8 authorises non-peaceful means if secession occurs or peaceful reunification is exhausted, and the white paper refuses to renounce force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One country, two systems is the core offer, with Article 5 allowing Taiwan to keep different systems and a high degree of autonomy.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent on religion, but PRC state doctrine places religious bodies under state and party supervision; inferred from that.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The doctrine does not address the head of state's role, and in the PRC the president is also the party leader.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The PRC is officially atheist and the white paper grounds legitimacy in national rejuvenation and the people, so divine rulership is inferred to be rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Unification doctrine has no tax position, but the PRC levies progressive income tax and Beijing's line favours state redistribution; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: No source addresses this; Marxist-influenced PRC doctrine stresses social conditions and education in forming people, which is the basis for this inference.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Beijing presents unification as grounded in law, such as the Anti-Secession Law and the constitution, and officially holds rulers to law; the inference is weak since party practice differs.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred from the white paper's link between national rejuvenation and national strength, and from the PRC's state-backed space programme.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The doctrine says nothing on this; PRC doctrine rejects Western checks and balances in favour of a single leading party, so rule by blending few and many is inferred to be disliked.

leader-cult.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent, and PRC official line is split between formal rejection of personality cults after Mao and heavy promotion of the paramount leader.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is unrelated to the doctrine and no position can be inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred from general PRC doctrine, which since 1978 no longer treats class struggle as the principal contradiction; the unification program itself is silent.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred: the unification offer promises Taiwan its own social and economic system, so redistribution is not part of it.

refugee-return.rationale: The unification doctrine does not address refugee return; no position can be inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: the white paper grounds the claim on Taiwan's history and on compatriots as one Chinese nation, though sovereignty rather than nationality is the formal basis.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: PRC law does not punish leaving a religion, and the unification program does not address it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred: PRC doctrine does not mandate religious dress and the unification program is silent.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred: under one country, two systems the region keeps its own currency, as Hong Kong did, so a shared currency is not Beijing's model.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from the white paper's emphasis on the shared kinship of compatriots across the strait, within a single state.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from PRC regional ethnic autonomy inside a unitary state, and its rejection of separate statehood.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The unification doctrine says nothing on minority strategy; no position can be inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred: the CCP's official Marxism holds that economic base conditions history, though the unification program does not state it.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is outside the unification doctrine; no position can be inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from state-led PRC economic policy, in which the state rescues key banks and enterprises.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: PRC doctrine rejects independent judicial checks on party-state authority, though the program does not address majority rule.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from PRC reserved seats and quotas for women in representative bodies; the unification program is silent.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from PRC integration into world trade; the program says nothing, though self-reliance is a state theme.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: Beijing has generally opposed attaching labor and environmental conditions to trade deals as interference.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: official doctrine mixes calls for dedication with material incentives, and the program is silent.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine seeks peaceful unification by state action and treats armed secession as illegal.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred: the PRC abolished titles and hereditary privilege, though the unification program does not address it.

history-own-civilization.rationale: PRC doctrine ties unification to national rejuvenation and state patriotic education, so nation-centred teaching is inferred as favoured.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Beijing frames its history with imperialism as a national humiliation and denounces colonial rule, so tutelage is inferred as rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: PRC policy stresses patriotic education about the nation, flag and anthem as part of national rejuvenation, and the white paper links it to the unification cause.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The unification program says nothing on racial preferences, and PRC ethnic policy preferences for minorities exist at home, so no clear line follows.

public-money-creation.rationale: The PRC state controls its banking system and the central bank, so public control of money is inferred as favoured; the unification doctrine itself is silent.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Official PRC doctrine holds that capitalism is dying only in the long run but has adapted so far, and the one country, two systems formula accommodates it; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Beijing denies any imperial aims and the unification doctrine addresses only Taiwan, though it cultivates ties in neighbouring regions; no clear line.

delink-world-market.rationale: PRC policy is integration into the world economy, so delinking is rejected as contrary to state policy; inferred from the reform and opening policy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: PRC state doctrine holds that workers share a common interest in socialism and does not endorse the labor-aristocracy view; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: PRC law bars discrimination in employment and public services, so a freedom to discriminate is inferred as rejected; the question is outside the doctrine.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The PRC rejects constitutional constraints on Party authority, and the unification doctrine says nothing on entrenched rights; inferred from state practice.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Beijing treats Taiwan's cession to Japan and the unequal treaties as illegitimate and holds that division was imposed from outside.

elective-rulers.rationale: PRC doctrine places rule with the Communist Party, not elected rulers; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: The Anti-Secession Law and white paper deny that Taiwan can decide separation alone.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: PRC doctrine upholds state authority and bars secession; inferred rejection of a right to resist rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The NPC is called the highest organ of state power, but the Party leads it; the unification doctrine is silent.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Unification doctrine says nothing about animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Standard PRC practice allows animal use for food and research; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: PRC doctrine stresses duty and national rejuvenation over withdrawal; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The doctrine does not address Western critical theory.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The doctrine does not address how rulers keep power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The unification doctrine does not address dependency theory.

party-own-road.rationale: Beijing presents its socialism as a path with Chinese characteristics, free of outside direction; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: PRC doctrine prizes self-reliance in development; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Beijing frames Taiwan's return after the 1895 cession as restoration of lost territory; inferred general principle.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Beijing's nationalism rests on the Han-majority state and national rejuvenation; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: PRC state doctrine rejects equating the two; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Deng's one country, two systems and official doctrine hold that China need not copy Western political systems.

military-guardian-role.rationale: PRC doctrine places the army under Party command and not as an independent political guardian; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent on family duty; PRC state doctrine draws on Confucian filial values and legally requires support of parents, so mild agreement is inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine: officials are appointed through party selection and a civil-service examination, not competitive elections; the white paper does not address it.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which screens foreign investment in strategic sectors and treats sovereignty over national assets as paramount.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from PRC state law, which permits divorce on mutual consent or breakdown of the marriage; the unification doctrine itself is silent.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from PRC democratic centralism, in which delegates are not bound by mandate or recallable at will by voters; the unification doctrine does not address it.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, where pensions rest on a state-run pooled system, with individual accounts only as a supplement.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, in which land is owned by the state or collectives and individuals hold only use rights; the Taiwan doctrine is silent.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from PRC constitutional practice, in which the National People's Congress formally approves the budget; the unification doctrine is silent.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which promotes standard Mandarin as the common language while formally protecting minority languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, under which land is state or collectively owned and foreigners cannot own it; the unification doctrine is silent.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which treats ethnic relations as harmonious and does not adopt outcome-based discrimination tests; the doctrine is silent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which treats consumption as a growth driver; the unification doctrine is silent, so mild disagreement is inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the white paper's insistence on non-interference in internal affairs, which Beijing applies as a general principle of foreign policy.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the white paper's and Article 3's rejection of outside interference, which Beijing frames as a general non-interference principle.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which has curbed large private companies, though the unification doctrine itself is silent.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine on foreign influence, which restricts foreign funding of NGOs; the unification texts do not address it.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from PRC policy of encouraging more births to counter population decline; not part of the unification doctrine.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: PRC land is state-owned and residence is controlled through hukou, but the doctrine does not address local purchase limits.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the PRC state's stress on employment and public works; the doctrine does not address it.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: Beijing rejects the promotion of Western-style democracy as interference and holds that regime type does not determine peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: PRC doctrine holds that law serves the state and the Party and citizens owe obedience.

non-intervention.rationale: Article 3 of the Anti-Secession Law and the 2022 white paper say the Taiwan question is internal and foreign interference will not be tolerated; non-interference is a core PRC principle.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: the state-run ACFTU is organised by industry, but the unification doctrine does not address unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: PRC state doctrine officially stresses unity of all ethnic groups and rejects such claims, apart from official attacks on separatists.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: PRC law and policy uphold marriage and the family as state institutions.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: PRC state doctrine limits public access to government information, with state secrets laws, despite open-information regulations.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: PRC policy stresses self-reliance in food and supply, but the doctrine does not address local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: PRC doctrine rests on the Party and the state, not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The white paper and Anti-Secession Law treat Taiwan as a purely domestic matter under Chinese law and reject outside courts or powers having a say.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred: the PRC is officially atheist and defines the nation as multi-ethnic and secular, not by religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Beijing's official line rejects hegemony and treats Taiwan as internal, not as a foreign tributary; inferred, and the statement's tribute model is not its doctrine.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: PRC fiscal practice is centrally pooled with transfers to poorer regions, though Hong Kong keeps its own finances; inferred from state doctrine.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: PRC state doctrine upholds public ownership of the main means of production alongside protected personal property; inferred, not stated in the unification texts.

defeat-communism.rationale: The doctrine is carried by a communist-led state, which offers coexistence under one country, two systems and does not aim to defeat communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: PRC practice lets private and public providers coexist within state-run systems; inferred, as unification texts are silent.

religion-illusion.rationale: The CCP holds a Marxist-atheist view of religion, but the unification doctrine is silent on it; inferred, mild agreement.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxist orthodoxy treats capitalism as historically progressive, and reform-era doctrine uses markets for development; inferred from state doctrine.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: PRC doctrine holds that women's liberation advances with socialist transformation; inferred, as unification texts do not discuss it.

socialized-care.rationale: PRC practice mixes state and family provision of care, and the unification doctrine has no position; adherents are split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Official PRC policy promotes standard Mandarin but does not purge foreign words broadly; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: The unification program treats Taiwan's status as internal and the state as sovereign over any arrangement, so treaties binding until both agree do not fit; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: PRC doctrine retains a state-led socialist economy and does not propose small property-owning communities; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: PRC policy has encouraged Han migration to minority regions, yet the unification doctrine has no stated position on settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The PRC claims to follow socialism with Chinese characteristics, so it does not frame itself as a third course apart from both; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The white paper grounds Taiwan's status in its long history as Chinese territory, though Beijing rests the claim mainly on sovereignty and law rather than a general principle favouring older ties.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The doctrine never addresses it; inferred from PRC state doctrine, which recognises the Holocaust and opposes fascism as part of its wartime narrative.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from general PRC law, which decriminalised homosexuality in 1997; the unification doctrine itself says nothing on it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred from general PRC state practice; the sources discuss only the ban on secessionist activity (Article 8) and Hong Kong's retained systems, not opposition in general.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from the PRC's official secularism; the doctrine does not address blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from PRC anti-imperialist doctrine, though unification itself treats Taiwan as part of China, not a colony.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Unrelated to the unification doctrine; no basis to infer a position.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from the PRC's secular state; the doctrine is silent on religious legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which favours party-led rule; one country, two systems also kept Hong Kong's institutions without extending direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from PRC official ideology, which stresses class and national rejuvenation over intersectional framing.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from general PRC policy, which offers limited legal recognition; the doctrine says nothing on it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from PRC law, which does not permit assisted dying; unrelated to the unification question.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The doctrine is a single-issue territorial position and takes no stance on the left-right division.

alienated-labor.rationale: Official PRC Marxism-Leninism uses the concept, but the unification doctrine does not address it and Deng's reforms accepted capitalism in Hong Kong.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which does not frame Islam against the West; the unification doctrine is silent.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred from the secular, Marxist-Leninist PRC state, which grounds authority in the party and the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from PRC secular state practice, which restricts religion in state institutions; the doctrine is silent.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Unrelated to the unification doctrine; no basis to infer a position.

social-market-economy.rationale: Beijing's own formula is a socialist market economy under state leadership, and Hong Kong keeps capitalism; neither fits the statement cleanly.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Anti-Secession Law authorises non-peaceful means and the white paper refuses to renounce force, so abolishing armed forces is incompatible.

rich-first.rationale: Deng, who devised one country, two systems, also framed reform as letting some regions get rich first; the sources here cover the formula, so this link is inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The doctrine demands that foreign powers not interfere over Taiwan but takes no position on the PRC's own bloc membership.

dynastic-succession.rationale: PRC doctrine is a party-state with non-hereditary leadership; inferred from general state doctrine, as unification doctrine is silent.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: State-owned banks, not user-owned mutual banks, are the PRC model; inferred from general state doctrine.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The 2022 white paper treats the question as purely internal and rejects outside pressure, so refusing foreign lender conditions is inferred as consistent.

property-franchise.rationale: The PRC officially claims universal suffrage and equal citizenship; a property qualification is inferred to be rejected.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Official doctrine promotes women's equality and ecological civilization but not this ecofeminist claim; the unification doctrine does not address it.

reification.rationale: Marxist theory underlies PRC doctrine but the unification doctrine is silent on it, so adherents are not clearly committed.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: PRC doctrine criticises capitalist 'bourgeois' freedoms as formal, so agreement is inferred; the unification doctrine itself is silent.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Anti-Secession Law shows the state claiming to act through enacted law, though party authority sits above it; inferred at low confidence.

racial-franchise.rationale: The white paper describes a multi-ethnic Chinese nation and equal rights for compatriots, so an ethnic franchise is inferred to be rejected.

online-participation.rationale: PRC doctrine promotes 'whole-process people's democracy' including online consultation; inferred from general state doctrine.

open-government-data.rationale: The state promotes some e-government transparency but controls information; the unification doctrine is silent.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Official doctrine proclaims freedom of religion and the state is secular; a restriction is inferred to be disfavoured.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Official doctrine stresses ethnic and religious unity of the nation; a boycott of a minority is inferred to be rejected.

citizens-assembly.rationale: PRC doctrine places political decisions with the Communist Party and its consultative bodies, not lot-chosen assemblies; inferred from general PRC state doctrine, not from the unification texts.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent on religion; PRC policy asks religions to adapt to socialist society, but this was not drawn from the unification sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which criticises extreme wealth gaps as contrary to common prosperity; the unification doctrine itself is silent.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The doctrine is a territorial one and says nothing; PRC practice is restrictive but adherents are not defined by it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The ruling party is officially atheist and promotes materialism in party education; inferred, low confidence.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: PRC doctrine stresses state security and public order; inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Beijing's model is a unitary state with one-party leadership rather than communal power-sharing; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: PRC doctrine gives the state the leading role in welfare and poverty alleviation; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: The 2018 removal of presidential term limits shows the official line disfavours them; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Delegated voting is foreign to the PRC's guided political system; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The doctrine is silent on existential risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious office is outside the doctrine and state-managed in the PRC; no stated position.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: PRC law formally declares equality of spouses; inferred from state doctrine, not unification.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from general PRC state doctrine, which treats citizenship as the basis of political rights and sovereignty as undivided.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which accepts heavy state regulation of housing; the Taiwan sources do not address it.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: the PRC has strengthened its IP law and treats protection of intellectual property as national policy.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from PRC practice, such as the Young Pioneers and military training, which organise youth for national purposes.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred: the PRC hosts no foreign nuclear weapons and opposes them near its territory.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine treats foreign interference in the Taiwan question as unacceptable and the PRC hosts no foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: PRC doctrine recognises the Nanjing Massacre but rejects genocide claims against itself, so official practice is split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from PRC socialist doctrine of distribution according to work, which coexists with a market economy.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The doctrine reserves force against secession and foreign interference, and no pacifist position is held.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The white paper presents the Chinese nation's continuity and shared history across the strait as the basis of unification.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which does not endorse this claim; the sources are silent.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from PRC state feminism, which works through the official women's federation; sources are silent.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from PRC practice, which officially honours martyrs of the revolution and the nation, though not as saints.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: the official ideology is atheist Marxism-Leninism, which treats politics as material struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The doctrine aims to gather Taiwan into the state, not to treat the homeland as a cultural centre for a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Unification is a state project, though the white paper also invokes shared culture and rejuvenation.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; the official atheist stance gives no position on how God is described.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: official doctrine stresses equality of nationalities and a state-led economy, not ethnic reservation, though it does emphasise Han-Chinese unity across the strait.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: In effect the doctrine holds that the Chinese people on both sides of the strait belong in one state, though framed as sovereignty rather than ethnic merger.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine: unions sit under the Party-led federation, which does not match independence from the state and party.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which describes the state as led by the working class and built on the alliance of workers and peasants.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which keeps public provision of basic services; the unification doctrine itself is silent.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred: the PRC legislature, the National People's Congress, is a single chamber, and the doctrine proposes no second one.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: PRC doctrine favours state and collective ownership under central direction, not community ownership by localities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine insists on a unitary state with the central government holding authority, which excludes confederal local decision.

family-wage.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent on wage policy.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent on ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which seeks state oversight of the financial system and payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which requires real-name registration online.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which puts national rejuvenation and the collective above individual claims.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred: PRC state doctrine is officially atheist but protects religion within limits, and the doctrine itself is silent.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The white paper and one country, two systems present Taiwan's autonomy as authorised by the central government, which can define and limit it.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which promotes science and agricultural technology; the unification doctrine itself is silent.

dense-cities.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent on urban form.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine speaks of one Chinese nation made of all its peoples, not of racial groups organising for separate interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred: the white paper ties unification to the pride and common ancestry of Chinese compatriots, so such pride is treated as legitimate.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Anti-Secession Law reserves non-peaceful means against secession, and Beijing treats Taiwan as internal, so it rejects limiting force to defence against attack.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Beijing's white paper rests unification on shared Chinese ancestry, history and culture across the Strait, treating the nation as one despite the political division.

communal-electorates.rationale: The PRC treats the Taiwan question as a matter of all Chinese people under one state and has no communal electorates; inferred from official doctrine.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The 2022 white paper says external forces, the US foremost, collude with separatists to divide China, and says Taiwan was split by civil war and foreign interference.

free-public-college.rationale: PRC public universities charge tuition and free tuition is not state policy; inferred from general PRC practice.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Single-issue unification doctrine; PRC environmental policy mixes taxes and regulation and the doctrine does not choose between them.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from general PRC state doctrine, which now stresses ecological civilisation; not part of the unification doctrine.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The doctrine says nothing on gender and values; inferred only from general PRC doctrine, which is not distinctive on this.

arms-reduction.rationale: The white paper stresses strengthening national defence as a curb on separatism and external interference, and force is not renounced, which tells against minimal arms.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The doctrine does not address openness of treaties; inferred as split between public diplomatic statements and confidential negotiation.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from general PRC state doctrine, which keeps controls on cross-border capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Unification doctrine has no gun policy; PRC state doctrine (s2) assumes the state's armed forces alone hold force, inferred from that.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Beijing reserves force against secession and foreign interference (s1, s2), so soldiers refusing orders would contradict it; but the statement is about wars between states, inferred only.

collective-bargaining.rationale: PRC doctrine has a single state-led union federation rather than independent bargaining; inferred from general PRC state doctrine, not from the unification texts.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent on income top-ups and general PRC doctrine offers no clear signal.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: State direction of the economy under PRC doctrine is hard to square with legally binding borrowing limits; inferred, low confidence.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: PRC state doctrine presents China as a developing country seeking a fairer international order; inferred, since the Taiwan texts do not cover it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The doctrine is built on defending and extending the existing state's sovereignty and the Communist Party's rule (s1, s2); inferred, though not stated as such.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: One country, two systems lets a region keep a different economic system (s4), but it is a fixed offer under one sovereign, not a general freedom for communities.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The unification texts do not address this and PRC doctrine on ecological civilisation is not documented in these sources.

sacred-nation.rationale: The white paper ties unification to national rejuvenation and the shared destiny of the Chinese nation across generations (s2), though it frames this as national rather than religious sanctity.

student-debt-relief.rationale: No bearing on the Taiwan question and no clear signal from PRC doctrine.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Beijing treats Taiwan and its regions as inseparable parts of one nation, not colonies (s2), and rejects colonial readings; inferred from that framing.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Nothing in the unification doctrine addresses human nature; PRC doctrine stresses sovereignty and development rights over universal rights.

public-service-media.rationale: PRC doctrine has state-controlled media rather than independent public media; inferred from general PRC state doctrine.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which is officially atheist and requires religions to adapt to the state; the sources do not discuss religious truth, so this is a low-confidence reading.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from general PRC state doctrine of state support for agriculture; the unification sources do not discuss farm prices.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred: the PRC keeps its nuclear arsenal and the white paper stresses building a strong national defence, so unilateral disarmament is not a plausible position.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: PRC doctrine rests on a single ruling party that claims to represent workers and the Anti-Secession framework leaves no room for independent opposition parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from PRC law, which prohibits harm to women's bodily rights; unification sources are silent on it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from PRC law, which gives women equal inheritance rights; unification sources are silent on it.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred: PRC doctrine treats the varieties of Chinese as one Chinese language and promotes Putonghua; the Wikipedia article stresses shared Chinese identity across the strait.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine of directing the economy and environment through administrative regulation, not private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: the PRC lets a party-state legislature make law with no chiefs' chamber, and the unification program does not mention customary leaders.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the PRC's state-led ecological civilization policy under which individual freedoms yield to state goals; the unification sources do not state it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The unification doctrine has no sentencing position and PRC adherents give no settled view in the sources.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from PRC promotion of standard Mandarin as the common national language and the white paper's stress on a shared national identity.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Unification doctrine never addresses union membership; inferred from PRC state doctrine, in which a single official union federation represents workers.

voter-id.rationale: The doctrine is silent on voter ID and mainland China has no competitive national elections, so no position is inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which recognises approved religions under state supervision without ranking interpretations; the unification doctrine itself is silent.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which defines democracy by outcomes ('whole-process democracy') rather than competitive elections; the unification doctrine itself is silent.

premarital-sex.rationale: The unification doctrine says nothing on sexual morality and PRC doctrine is not clearly committed either way.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which asserts state control of the internet for stability; the unification doctrine itself is silent.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which favours state-provided welfare programmes over a replacement cash scheme.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from PRC law, which grants women equal political rights; the unification doctrine itself is silent.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed by the unification doctrine; PRC Marxist tradition is critical of religion but does not single it out as a main cause.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the unification doctrine; PRC doctrine officially recognises ethnic nationalities, so no clear position is inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which maintains state bodies for women's affairs; the unification doctrine itself is silent.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from general PRC state doctrine of state ownership of land; the unification sources do not address it.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from Beijing's rejection of outside jurisdiction over its internal affairs, which the white paper stresses for Taiwan.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the PRC being an officially atheist state; the sources never address scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which formally promotes gender equality in regional autonomy.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which defends its socialist state against foreign pressure.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the PRC's people's congress system, in which higher bodies are elected by lower ones.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the PRC's state-controlled religion policy, which gives no church special status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The PRC's ethnic regional autonomy system and the high autonomy offered under one country, two systems both endorse such arrangements within one state (s4, s1).

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Article 3 of the Anti-Secession Law and the white paper say the Taiwan question is for all Chinese people to settle, which excludes a vote by the territory's inhabitants alone.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from PRC opposition to redrawing borders inherited from history, a position the unification sources do not discuss.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine, which is a single territorial issue.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from PRC settlement policy in minority regions; the sources do not address it.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed by the unification doctrine; PRC law is formally gender neutral but practice differs.

missingStatements.text: A country may use military force to prevent a region from separating from it.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 8 authorises non-peaceful means if secession occurs or peaceful reunification is exhausted, and the white paper refuses to renounce force.

missingStatements.text: A region could join a larger state while keeping its own economic and legal system and a high degree of autonomy.
missingStatements.rationale: One country, two systems is the core offer, with Article 5 allowing Taiwan to keep different systems and a high degree of autonomy.

missingStatements.text: Whether a region belongs to a country should be settled by the country as a whole, not by a vote of that region alone.
missingStatements.rationale: The white paper and Article 3 call the Taiwan question an internal matter for all Chinese people, which excludes a Taiwanese-only decision.

missingStatements.text: Foreign governments should not interfere in the dispute over a territory's status.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 3 and the white paper say no outside interference will be tolerated in resolving the Taiwan question.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Taiwan dispute; foreign non-interference is not a defining position beyond it and is covered loosely by end-foreign-alliances and dominated-front.

notes: Taiwanese pro-unification strands, especially within the KMT, would answer differently: they favour the ROC framework and reject one country, two systems. Most Taiwanese polls show little support for unification. Unification is a single-issue doctrine, so many answers are inferred from wider PRC state doctrine.
